title: Drop-In Tech Support Hours
shortDescription: No appointment needed — bring your Blackboard, Zoom, or classroom tech questions to our weekly virtual drop-in.
longDescription: Open drop-in hours over Zoom for quick tech questions — no appointment or registration needed. For longer or more involved issues, book a full appointment instead.

title: Spring 2027 Course Design Institute
shortDescription: A three-day intensive for faculty rebuilding a course from the ground up, culminating in a completed course shell.
longDescription:
An application-based, three-day intensive over winter break for faculty substantially redesigning a course. Participants leave with a built course shell, an assessment plan, and a peer feedback partner for the semester.

Application required; space is limited to 15 faculty.

title: Peer Observation Program Info Session
shortDescription: Learn how the redesigned peer observation program works before opting in for spring.
longDescription: An overview of the redesigned, growth-oriented peer observation program — what a cycle looks like, how pairs are matched, and how observation notes are (and aren't) used. Optional participation opens after this session.

title: UDL in Practice: Book Club Kickoff
shortDescription: First meeting of a semester-long book club working through Universal Design for Learning in Higher Ed.
longDescription: Kickoff session for a five-part book club. Copies of the book are available at the CTL front desk while supplies last. Future sessions will be scheduled with the group at this first meeting.
eventLocation: CTL Workshop Room, Old Main 210 & Zoom (hybrid)

title: Mid-Year Assessment Check-In
shortDescription: A hybrid working session to review how mid-semester feedback data is being used across departments.
longDescription: Department representatives reviewed anonymized mid-semester feedback trends and discussed what's changing as a result heading into fall planning.

title: New Faculty Orientation: Fall Kickoff
shortDescription: A half-day orientation covering course design support, LMS basics, and how to get help from the CTL.
longDescription:
Required orientation session for all new tenure-track and full-time non-tenure-track faculty starting this fall. Covers CTL services, LMS fundamentals, and how to request a course design consultation.

Lunch provided.

title: Annual Teaching & Learning Conference
shortDescription: Our flagship two-day conference featuring a keynote, breakout sessions, and a poster showcase from campus faculty.
longDescription:
The Annual Teaching & Learning Conference returns for a second day this year, with a keynote address, over a dozen faculty-led breakout sessions, and a poster showcase highlighting classroom research from across campus.

Registration is now full; join the waitlist to be notified of any openings.
eventLocation: Corey Union, Function Room & Various Breakout Rooms

title: Grading for Growth: A Hands-On Workshop
shortDescription: Bring an assignment and leave with a revised resubmission policy you can use next semester.
longDescription:
A working session building directly on our Grading for Growth guide. Participants bring a current assignment and rubric and leave with a draft resubmission policy, revision memo template, and a grading-load estimate.

Laptops recommended. Limited to 20 participants for hands-on support.

title: Spring Open House
shortDescription: Drop by the CTL to meet the team, tour the space, and learn what we offer for the coming semester.
longDescription: An informal open house welcoming faculty and staff to the newly renovated Center for Teaching and Learning space. Light refreshments provided; no RSVP required to attend, but registering helps us plan.

longDescription: Faculty from across departments shared how they are handling AI use in their courses this semester — what's working, what isn't, and where policies still feel unsettled. No slides, no recording, just conversation.

title: Next Years Workshop Testing
shortDescription: Whether you are versed in Universal Design for Learning (UDL) or new to that framework, please join Gillian Mertens and Kati Ahern for a two-day, in-person workshop on how to bring UDL into Online Teaching.
longDescription:
Whether you are versed in Universal Design for Learning (UDL) or new to that framework, please join Gillian Mertens and Kati Ahern for a two-day, in-person workshop on how to bring UDL into Online Teaching.

Whether you are versed in Universal Design for Learning (UDL) or new to that framework, please join Gillian Mertens and Kati Ahern for a two-day, in-person workshop on how to bring UDL into Online Teaching. Gillian and Kati will co-facilitate an interactive exploration for how to intentionally design online course experiences (both synchronous and asynchronous) with attention to a variety of means of engagement, representation, and expression in the process of learning.

The workshop will include a Brightspace site with resources, activities, and support, as well as lots of practical, participant-led brainstorming for how to design with diverse learners, access needs, and playfulness and JOY in mind.

This is a two-day series brought to you by the Center for Teaching and Learning and Co-facilitated by Gillian Mertens and Kati Ahern.
oppLaborExpectation: Attend both workshop days in-person from 9am-3pm.
